authorityBoundary: Current public-source status and exact-site historical context only. This record is not a statutory planning determination, legal-boundary opinion, measured survey, structural opinion or property-level flood conclusion.

sources.title: Review of the Bromley Local Plan
observed: The adopted Bromley Local Plan 2019 remains under review.
The council records the 2025 Direction of Travel as its second Regulation 18 consultation.
The current review surface does not establish a replacement Local Plan as adopted development-plan policy.
sources.authorityBoundary: Official source/status evidence only; it does not assign proposal-specific planning weight.

sources.title: Direction of Travel Consultation July to September 2025
observed: The Direction of Travel consultation ran from 25 July to 26 September 2025.
The council explicitly states that the Direction of Travel document does not contain draft policies.
The next stage described by the council is preparation of a Submission Draft Local Plan.
sources.authorityBoundary: The Direction of Travel is emerging plan-making material, not operative development-plan policy.

sources.title: Draft London Plan consultation
observed: Consultation on the Draft London Plan closed at 17:00 on 15 October 2026.
Examination in public is scheduled for 2027 and adoption for 2028.
The Draft London Plan is therefore not the adopted London spatial development strategy at this gate.
sources.authorityBoundary: Official strategic source/status evidence only; no scalar material weight is inferred.

sources.title: National Planning Policy Framework — DM4 Emerging development plan proposals
observed: Relevant emerging-plan policies may be given weight according to stage of preparation, unresolved objections and compliance with national plan-making policy.
The policy does not provide a universal numeric weight.
Proposal-specific weight remains a decision-maker judgement.
sources.authorityBoundary: National policy supplies the weighting factors, not a native project planning determination.

sources.title: Flood risk: postcode search tool data
observed: The Environment Agency publishes the postcode flood-risk dataset as open data.
The tool reports counts of properties in high, medium and low long-term flood-risk areas for a postcode and directs users to the address-level GOV.UK service.
Risk is for the area around an address/property, not a property-specific guarantee.
The exact BR2 8LN authoritative row could not be acquired by the T9 automated execution path; no secondary mirror is promoted in its place.
sources.authorityBoundary: Competent high-level public source identified; exact control-postcode result remains pending authoritative byte/row recovery.

sources.title: 41 Lennard Road planning statement — history of 23/00297/FULL6
observed: The exact-site 23/00297/FULL6 proposal was refused on 21 March 2024.
The reproduced refusal reason identified design and inadequate side space, disproportion to the host dwelling, dominance relative to the row, visual amenity and street-scene harm.
The reproduced reason cites Bromley Local Plan Policies 6, 8 and 37 and London Plan Policy D3.
sources.authorityBoundary: Proposal-specific historical context from a public planning-document copy. It is not transferred into a refusal of the different Reference House candidate and is not treated as the official decision notice itself.

sources.title: DPL-T3/T4 authored Reference House placement
observed: The unchanged Reference House canonical front is constructed 26.0 m inward from the admitted screening frontage midpoint, plus a 4.5 m along-frontage offset.
The placement is street-facing but materially inland from the frontage rather than a simple street-line replacement.
Indicative title-index side clearances are below the Bromley Policy 8 one-metre numeric floor on both sides, but the title-index polygon is not legal or measured boundary evidence.
sources.authorityBoundary: Current controlled project geometry; does not itself decide planning acceptability.

interpretiveRules: Emerging-source status may be resolved from official sources without pretending to assign a statutory scalar planning weight.
A prior refusal on a different proposal is positive site/context evidence but not a reusable refusal rule.
The exact-site prior side-space/street-scene refusal and the authored 26 m inward placement make local/strategic design-context judgement genuinely decision-critical rather than safely self-passable.
The official Environment Agency postcode dataset must be recovered directly before flood screening is discharged; secondary postcode mirrors are not substitutes.
No source in this record authorises Reference House mutation, route search, whole-site compatibility or incompatibility.
